lesson: Momentum should follow repricing, not changes in who is listed: skipping the shift when the provider count changed on the day of the last rise gives DEV +0.0036 and HOLDOUT +0.0008 over exp_004, and was better in 6 of 6 weeks (Sep 15-Oct 26, overlapping the selection windows). Partial reversion after composition moves lowered DEV in all 18 settings tried: rejected before the gate. Gain is within noise; adopted because the pre-registered rule chose it. Sunday file changes only in q10 of 19 rows (at most 0.5%).

spec._hypothesis: DEVIN_NEXT.md task A: when the GetDeploying weekly median for the same GPU and pricing mode sits above our last value, our series tends to move up within 7 days, and vice versa. DEV EDA: Spearman(log gap, exp_007 residual) +0.11 overall, +0.17 at h=7. DEV sweep (scratch/dev_sweep_aggregator*.py): shifting all three quantiles lowered DEV in all 40 settings (the median must stay on the last value for step series); moving only the interval edge on the gap's side raised DEV; beta_agg=0.1, cap=0.1 is the best setting that raises all three DEV metrics (pooled, median, geomean).

reason: dev skill_pooled +0.0056 vs champion exp_007 (need >= +0.002); holdout +0.0011 (need >= -0.0)
lesson: The GetDeploying weekly median carries a weak lead only as interval-edge information: moving the median toward it lowered DEV in every one of 40 settings, while moving just the q90 up (aggregator above) or q10 down (below) by 0.1*clip(log gap, +-0.1) gave DEV +0.0056 and HOLDOUT +0.0011 over exp_007. Per-series Wilcoxon: DEV 24/37 better p=0.049, HOLDOUT 20/37 p=0.14. Passes the gate but is within noise; parameters picked from 64 DEV settings, so the DEV gain is optimistic.
